name: Kitadake loop from Hirogawara (北岳)
why: Japan's second-highest mountain, 3,193 m: up through forest and the Kusasuberi meadows to a hut on the ridge, sunrise over Mount Fuji from the top, then down past the snowy Daikanba valley.
book: No permit. Yamanashi Kotsu bus from Kofu station (south exit) to Hirogawara, about 2 hours, only from late June to early November; by car, park at Ashiyasu and take the forest-road bus. Book Kitadake Katanokoya (or Shiraneoike-goya) ahead.
water: Drinking water at Hirogawara and Shiraneoike-goya; on the ridge it is sold at Katanokoya. Carry 2 litres for the Kusasuberi climb.
dangers: Kusasuberi is a long, steep climb of about 800 m: go slowly in the heat of the day.
Above 2,800 m there is no shelter from wind and lightning: be at the hut by early afternoon.
Snow can stay in the Daikanba valley into July and come back in October; in winter this is a mountaineering route.
Altitude above 3,000 m: headaches on the first night are common.
turnaround: Not at Shiraneoike-goya by 14:30 on day 1: sleep there instead and climb Kusasuberi the next morning.

points.name: Hirogawara
points.note: The bus terminal at about 1,520 m. Cross the suspension bridge over the Noro river and climb into old forest.

points.name: Shiraneoike-goya
points.note: The hut by a small pond at 2,230 m, after about 2.5 hours. Above it the Kusasuberi grass slope climbs straight up to the ridge.

points.name: Kitadake Katanokoya
points.note: Night 1 at about 3,000 m on the shoulder of Kitadake, where the Kotaro ridge joins. Sunset over the Northern and Central Alps.

points.name: Kitadake summit
points.note: 3,193 m, about 30 minutes up the ridge from the hut. Mount Fuji to the east, Ainodake on the ridge south.

points.name: Happonba col
points.note: Down the summit scree to this col, then steep wooden ladders and steps into the Daikanba valley, past Futamata and back to Hirogawara.
